metadata.title: Orthogonal Transfer for Multitask Optimization
metadata.authors: Sheng-Hao Wu, Zhi-Hui Zhan, Kay Chen Tan, Jun Zhang
metadata.venue_year: IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation, vol. 27(1), Feb 2023 (accepted Mar 2022)

tldr: OTMTO improves knowledge transfer in evolutionary multitask optimization for tasks of different dimensionalities, via an optimization-based cross-task mapping (CTM) plus orthogonal-experimental-design transfer (OT) that learns which dimensions to combine.

problem.problem: Knowledge transfer (KT) in evolutionary multitask optimization (EMTO) struggles when tasks have different dimensionalities (DDs) and when dimensions differ in importance/similarity (Sec. I).
problem.motivation: Existing unified-solution-representation methods pad redundant dimensions, causing negative transfer across heterogeneous spaces, and uniform-probability crossover transfers low-quality dimensions (Sec. II-C).

method.core_idea: Operate KT in each task's original search space: map the source task's global-best to the target space (CTM), then use orthogonal experimental design to find the best combination of dimensions between the mapped individual and a random target individual (OT) (Sec. III).
method.how_it_works: CTM frames mapping as an inner optimization solved by DE/best/1 aligning kNN-style hypotheses of source/target (Sec. III-B, Alg. 1). OT applies OED needing M=2^ceil(log2(D+1)) evaluations instead of exponential (Sec. III-C, Alg. 2). CDT transfers across similar dimensions via KL-divergence similarity + roulette (Sec. III-D, Alg. 3). pOT and pCDT are adapted by a reward rule (Eq. 11, 14).
method.assumptions: Tasks share some exploitable similarity; base solver is DE/rand/1; KT benefit is approximated by the immediate replacement reward.

datasets: Proposed MTOP-DD benchmark (144 problems, D in {20,30,40,50})
key_results: On CEC17, significantly better than MFEA on 16/18 tasks (worse on 1) and better than MFEA2 on 15 (Table II)
Better than MTGA on 12 tasks, worse on 1 (Table II)
On MTOP-DD, outperforms MFEA/MFEA2/EMTEA/MTGA on most tasks; EMTEA sometimes worse than single-task SODE, evidencing negative transfer (Table III)
Component ablations support CTM, OT, and CDT (Tables IV-V)
Higher DPB success rates than SODE/EMTEA/MTGA (Table VI)

contributions: CTM: an optimization-based mapping enabling KT across tasks with different dimensionalities in their original spaces.
OT: using orthogonal experimental design to learn the best dimension combination with few extra evaluations.
CDT: similarity-based cross-dimension transfer using KL-divergence.
Reward-based adaptive control of KT intensity (pOT, pCDT).
A new configurable MTOP-DD benchmark test suite.

strengths: Targets an under-studied and realistic setting (different task dimensionalities) and contributes a reusable benchmark beyond the method itself.
Broad evaluation: standard CEC17 + new MTOP-DD + real-world DPB + 3/5-task scalability, with Wilcoxon significance over 20 runs.
Thorough ablations isolate each component (CTM mapping alternatives, OT vs SBX/UBX, CDT vs intratask sampling) (Tables IV-V).
Provides a theoretical reading of CTM as aligning kNN hypotheses of the two tasks (Sec. III-B2).
weaknesses: No code release was found, so reproduction relies on reimplementing an intricate multi-component algorithm.
Much evidence (other D combinations, the quantitative CEC17 metric analysis, running time) lives in supplementary material, limiting what the main text alone can verify.
Baselines reflect the ~2021 EMTO family; gains versus more recent EMTO methods are not established.
CTM runs an inner DE optimization (maxINFE=500) per transfer; the wall-clock/overhead trade-off vs simpler methods is only partly addressed (running time deferred to supplementary).
Main tables foreground mean fitness and win/tie/loss counts; variance/effect sizes are not prominently reported.
open_questions: How does OTMTO scale to high dimensionality and many tasks given the per-transfer inner-optimization cost? (the authors flag this as future work)
Does the kNN-hypothesis-alignment view predict when CTM fails for highly dissimilar tasks?
Do the gains persist with base solvers other than DE/rand/1?

reproducibility.compute_reported: FE budgets and full parameter settings are given (maxFE=1000xDi, maxINFE=500, ps=100, etc.); running time and some benchmark data are in supplementary; no hardware details in the main text.
reproducibility.notes: Detailed pseudocode (Alg. 1-4) and parameter tables make reimplementation feasible, but the absence of released code plus supplementary-only results raises practical risk.

positioning: Extends the EMTO line from MFEA (single-population, unified representation, implicit KT) toward multipopulation, explicit, dimension-aware KT in original search spaces. Differentiates from autoencoder mappings (EMTEA, kernelized AE) and random dimension shuffling (MTGA) via optimization-based mapping (CTM) and OED-based dimension combination (OT); claims to be the first to use OED for cross-task KT.
follow_up_reading: Gupta et al. 2016 (MFEA) [22] - the baseline paradigm this work departs from.
Bali et al. 2020 (MFEA-II) [33] - online similarity estimation for when-to-transfer.
Feng et al. (EMTEA, explicit autoencoding) [28] - the autoencoder mapping OTMTO contrasts with.
Da et al. 2016 (CEC17 benchmark) [65] - the benchmark and performance metric used.
